alexandrapalace|londonengland.name: Alexandra Palace
alexandrapalace|londonengland.extract: Alexandra Palace is an entertainment and sports venue in north London, situated between Wood Green and Muswell Hill in the London Borough of Haringey. A Grade II listed building, it is built on the site of Tottenham Wood and the later Tottenham Wood Farm.

allentheater|clevelandoh.name: Allen Theater
allentheater|clevelandoh.extract: Playhouse Square is a theater district in downtown Cleveland, Ohio, United States. It is the largest performing arts center in the US outside of New York City (only Lincoln Center is larger).

alpinevalleymusictheater|easttroywi.name: Alpine Valley Music Theater
alpinevalleymusictheater|easttroywi.extract: Alpine Valley Music Theatre is a 30,000-capacity amphitheater located on County Highway D in East Troy, Wisconsin. The seasonal venue was built in 1977 and it features a wooden roof, covering the 7,500-seat pavilion and a sprawling lawn.

alumnistadiumuniversityofmassachusetts|a.wikiTitle: Campus of the University of Massachusetts Amherst
alumnistadiumuniversityofmassachusetts|a.extract: The campus of the University of Massachusetts Amherst is located mostly in Amherst, Massachusetts, United States, with a portion located in Hadley. Founded on 310 acres (130 ha) in rural Western Massachusetts, the campus has grown to nearly 1,450 acres.

americanstudios|hollywoodca.name: American Studios
americanstudios|hollywoodca.extract: Universal Studios Hollywood is a film studio and theme park located in Universal City, California, United States, near Hollywood, Los Angeles. Owned by NBCUniversal (Comcast) and operated by Universal Destinations & Experiences, it is one of the oldest and most famous Hollywood film studios still in use.

auditoriumcoliseum|jacksonvillefl.name: Auditorium Coliseum
auditoriumcoliseum|jacksonvillefl.extract: The Jacksonville Veterans Memorial Coliseum (originally and still commonly known as the Jacksonville Coliseum) was a multi-purpose arena located in Jacksonville, Florida. Built in 1960 and known as "northern Florida's most historic concert venue", it was home to most of the city's indoor professional sports teams and it hosted various concerts, circuses, and other events.

auditoriumtheater|chicagoil.name: Auditorium Theater
auditoriumtheater|chicagoil.extract: The Auditorium Building is a structure at the northwest corner of South Michigan Avenue and  Ida B. Wells Drive in the Loop community area of Chicago, Illinois, United States. Completed in 1889, it is one of the best-known designs of Louis Sullivan and Dankmar Adler.

augustaciviccenter|augustame.name: Augusta Civic Center
augustaciviccenter|augustame.extract: The Augusta Civic Center is a convention center located in Augusta, Maine. It has a total of 49,000 square feet (4,600 m2) and 26 rooms.

autzenstadiumuniversityoforegon|eugeneor.name: Autzen Stadium (University Of Oregon)
autzenstadiumuniversityoforegon|eugeneor.extract: Autzen Stadium is an outdoor football stadium in Eugene, Oregon, United States. Located north of the University of Oregon campus, it is the home field of the Oregon Ducks of the Big Ten Conference.

avalonballroom|sanfranciscoca.name: Avalon Ballroom
avalonballroom|sanfranciscoca.extract: The Avalon Ballroom was a music venue in the Polk Gulch neighborhood of San Francisco, California, at 1244 Sutter Street (or 1268 Sutter, depending on the entrance). The space is known as the location of many concerts of the counterculture movement, from around 1966 to 1969.

baltimoreciviccenter|baltimoremd.name: Baltimore Civic Center
baltimoreciviccenter|baltimoremd.extract: The Great Baltimore Fire raged in Baltimore, Maryland from Sunday February 7 to Monday February 8, 1904. More than 1,500 buildings were completely leveled, and some 1,000 severely damaged, bringing property loss from the disaster to an estimated $100 million, or $3.6 billion in 2026.

bartonhallcornelluniversity|ithacany.name: Barton Hall (Cornell University)
bartonhallcornelluniversity|ithacany.extract: Barton Hall is an on-campus field house on the campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York.  It is the site of the school's indoor track facilities, ROTC offices and classes, and Cornell Police.

berkeleycommunitytheater|berkeleyca.name: Berkeley Community Theater
berkeleycommunitytheater|berkeleyca.extract: Berkeley Community Theater is a theater located in Berkeley, California, United States, on the campus of Berkeley High School. The theater is administered by the Berkeley Unified School District.

bickershawfestival|wiganengland.name: Bickershaw Festival
bickershawfestival|wiganengland.extract: The Bickershaw Festival was a rock festival held in Bickershaw, Lancashire, England, between 5 and 7 May 1972. Except for the 1976–1979 Deeply Vale Festivals, Bickershaw was the only major north-west multi-day festival with camping.

billericaforum|billericama.name: Billerica Forum
billericaforum|billericama.extract: North Billerica is an unincorporated village of the town of Billerica, Massachusetts, United States, one of the nine sections (hamlets) that make up the Town of Billerica. It is the home to Faulkner and Talbot mills and the North Billerica Train Depot.

birminghamjeffersonciviccentercoliseum|b.name: Birmingham-Jefferson Civic Center Coliseum
birminghamjeffersonciviccentercoliseum|b.extract: The Birmingham–Jefferson Convention Complex (formerly known as Birmingham-Jefferson Civic Center) is an entertainment, sports, and convention complex located in the heart of Birmingham, Alabama's Uptown Entertainment District. The Sheraton Birmingham and Westin Birmingham are located on the campus adjoining the convention center.

bostongarden|bostonma.name: Boston Garden
bostongarden|bostonma.extract: The Boston Garden was an arena in Boston, Massachusetts. Designed by boxing promoter Tex Rickard, who also built the third iteration of New York's Madison Square Garden, it opened on November 17, 1928, as "Boston Madison Square Garden" (later shortened to just "Boston Garden") and outlived its original namesake by 30 years.

bostonmusichall|bostonma.name: Boston Music Hall
bostonmusichall|bostonma.extract:
The Boston Music Hall was a concert hall located on Winter Street in Boston, Massachusetts, with an additional entrance on Hamilton Place.
One of the oldest continuously operating theaters in the United States, it was built in 1852 and was the original home of the Boston Symphony Orchestra.

bostonteaparty|bostonma.name: Boston Tea Party
bostonteaparty|bostonma.extract: The Boston Tea Party was an act of protest that took place on December 16, 1773, during the American Revolution. Initiated by the Sons of Liberty in Boston, the capital of Massachusetts, one of the Thirteen Colonies of British America, it escalated tensions between Great Britain and the Patriots, who opposed British policy towards its American colonies.

cafeaugogo|newyorkcityny.name: Cafe au Go-Go
cafeaugogo|newyorkcityny.extract: The Cafe Au Go Go was a night club in Greenwich Village located in the basement of the New Andy Warhol Garrick Theatre building in the late 1960s, at 152 Bleecker Street in Manhattan, New York City. The club featured many musical groups, folk singers and comedy acts between the opening in February 1964 until closing in December 1970.

calexpoamphitheater|sacramentoca.name: Cal Expo Amphitheater
calexpoamphitheater|sacramentoca.extract: The California Exposition and State Fair (Cal Expo) is an independent state agency established by law in the California Food and Agriculture codes. Cal Expo is governed by an appointed 11-member Board of Directors and daily operations are managed by the chief executive officer (selected by the Board).

cameronindoorstadiumdukeuniversity|durha.name: Cameron Indoor Stadium (Duke University)
cameronindoorstadiumdukeuniversity|durha.extract: Cameron Indoor Stadium is an indoor arena located on the campus of Duke University in Durham, North Carolina. The 9,314-seat facility is the primary indoor athletic venue for the Duke Blue Devils and serves as the home court for Duke men's and women's basketball and women's volleyball.

camprandallfieldhouseuofwi|madisonwi.name: Camp Randall Field House, U. Of Wi.
camprandallfieldhouseuofwi|madisonwi.extract: The Wisconsin Field House (commonly known as the UW Field House) is a multi-purpose arena owned by the University of Wisconsin–Madison and located directly south of Camp Randall Stadium. In addition to sports events, the Field House has been the site of large community gatherings such as convocations and concerts.

capecodcoliseum|southyarmouthma.name: Cape Cod Coliseum
capecodcoliseum|southyarmouthma.extract: Cape Cod Coliseum was a multi-purpose arena located off White's Path in South Yarmouth, Massachusetts. In addition to sporting events, the coliseum hosted rock concerts.

capitalcentre|landovermd.extract: Capital Center or Capital Centre may refer to:

capitoltheater|passaicnj.name: Capitol Theater
capitoltheater|passaicnj.extract: The Capitol Theatre is a historic theater located in the village of Port Chester, Westchester County, New York. It was designed by noted theater architect Thomas W. Lamb (1871–1942) and built in 1926.

capitoltheater|portchesterny.name: Capitol Theater
capitoltheater|portchesterny.extract: The Capitol Theatre is a historic theater located in the village of Port Chester, Westchester County, New York. It was designed by noted theater architect Thomas W. Lamb (1871–1942) and built in 1926.

carouselballroom|sanfranciscoca.name: Carousel Ballroom
carouselballroom|sanfranciscoca.extract: The Fillmore West was a historic live rock and roll music venue in San Francisco, California, US, which became famous under the direction of concert promoter Bill Graham from 1968 to 1971. Named after The Fillmore at the intersection of Fillmore Street and Geary Boulevard (which was Graham's principal venue from 1966 to 1968), it stood at the southwest corner of Market Street and South Van Ness Avenue in the Civic Center district.

cityhall|newcastleengland.name: City Hall
cityhall|newcastleengland.extract: The Newcastle City Hall (currently known as O2 City Hall Newcastle for sponsorship reasons) is a concert hall located in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. It has hosted many popular music and classical artists throughout the years, as well as standup and comedy acts.

civicarena|pittsburghpa.name: Civic Arena
civicarena|pittsburghpa.extract: The Civic Arena, formerly the Civic Auditorium and later Mellon Arena, was a multi-purpose arena located in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It primarily served as the home to the Pittsburgh Penguins, the city's National Hockey League (NHL) franchise, from 1967 to 2010.

civicauditorium|sanjoseca.name: Civic Auditorium
civicauditorium|sanjoseca.extract: The San Jose Civic (formerly known as the San Jose Civic Auditorium and City National Civic) is a former arena, currently operating as a theatre and concert venue, located in downtown San Jose, California. The venue is owned by the City of San Jose, is managed by Team San Jose and is booked by Nederlander Concerts.

civiccenter|roanokeva.name: Civic Center
civiccenter|roanokeva.extract: Berglund Center (originally called the Roanoke Civic Center) is a 10,500-seat multi-purpose arena located in the Williamson Road neighborhood of Roanoke, Virginia. It was built in 1971 and is currently the home of the Roanoke Rail Yard Dawgs of the SPHL.  The arena also hosts Virginia Tech, Radford University and Roanoke College men's ice hockey games, as well as regular concerts and other large indoor events.

civichall|rotterdamnetherlands.extract: This is a chronological list of houses, commercial buildings and other works by Marcel Breuer.

clevelandpublichall|clevelandoh.name: Cleveland Public Hall
clevelandpublichall|clevelandoh.extract: The Cleveland Public Library is a public library system in Cleveland, Ohio. Founded in 1869, it had a circulation of 3.5 million items in 2020.

clubagora|columbusoh.name: Club Agora
clubagora|columbusoh.extract:
The Agora Theatre and Ballroom (commonly known as the Cleveland Agora, or simply, the Agora) is a music venue located in Cleveland, Ohio.
Hank LoConti opened the first Agora on February 27, 1966, near the campus of Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland.

coboarena|detroitmi.name: COBO Arena
coboarena|detroitmi.extract: Huntington Place (formerly known as Cobo Hall, Cobo Center, and briefly TCF Center) is a convention center in Downtown Detroit, owned by the Detroit Regional Convention Facility Authority (DRCFA) and operated by Legends Global. Located at 1 Washington Boulevard, the facility was originally named after former Mayor of Detroit Albert Cobo.

comptonterraceamphitheater|tempeaz.name: Compton Terrace Amphitheater
comptonterraceamphitheater|tempeaz.extract: Compton Terrace was a name given to two former outdoor amphitheaters for concerts, located in the Phoenix metropolitan area of Arizona. It was named in honor of a local radio personality and music promoter, William Edward Compton.

concertgebouw|amsterdamnetherlands.name: Concertgebouw
concertgebouw|amsterdamnetherlands.extract: The Royal Concertgebouw (Dutch: het Koninklijk Concertgebouw, pronounced [ət ˈkoːnɪŋklə kɔnˈsɛrtxəˌbʌu]) is a concert hall in Amsterdam, Netherlands. The Dutch term "concertgebouw" translates into English as "concert building".

coppscoliseum|hamiltonontariocanada.name: Copps Coliseum
coppscoliseum|hamiltonontariocanada.extract: TD Coliseum (formerly Copps Coliseum and FirstOntario Centre) is a sports and entertainment arena at the corner of Bay Street North and York Boulevard in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. Opened in 1985 as Copps Coliseum, it has a capacity of up to 18,000.

crislerarenauniversityofmichigan|annarbo.name: Crisler Arena (University Of Michigan)
crislerarenauniversityofmichigan|annarbo.extract: Crisler Center (formerly known as the University Events Building and Crisler Arena) is an indoor basketball arena located on the campus of the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor. It serves as the home arena for the men's and women's basketball teams, as well as the women's gymnastics team at the university.

crystalballroom|portlandor.name: Crystal Ballroom
crystalballroom|portlandor.extract: Crystal Ballroom, originally built as Cotillion Hall, is a historic building on Burnside Street in Portland, Oregon, United States. Cotillion Hall was built in 1914 as a ballroom, and dance revivals were held there through the Great Depression.

cumberlandcountyciviccenter|portlandme.name: Cumberland County Civic Center
cumberlandcountyciviccenter|portlandme.extract: Cumberland County is a county in the U.S. state of Maine. As of the 2020 census, the population was 303,069, making it the most populous county in Maine.

curtishixonconventionhall|tampafl.name: Curtis Hixon Convention Hall
curtishixonconventionhall|tampafl.extract: Curtis Hixon Hall was an indoor sports arena, convention center, concert venue, and special events center which was located at 600 Ashley Drive along the Hillsborough River in downtown Tampa, Florida. Named after Curtis Hixon, a long-time Tampa mayor who died in 1956 during his fourth term in the office, it opened in 1965 and was the primary concert, indoor sports, and civic gathering place for the city for about twenty years.

danecountycoliseum|madisonwi.name: Dane County Coliseum
danecountycoliseum|madisonwi.extract: Alliant Energy Center is a multi-building complex located in Madison, Wisconsin. It comprises 164 acres (0.66 km2) of greenspace and includes the 255,000-square-foot (23,700 m2) Exhibition Hall, the 10,000-seat Veterans Memorial Coliseum, the 29-acre (0.12 km2) Willow Island, several multi-use pavilions, and the 22,000-square-foot (2,000 m2) Arena.

deercreekamphitheater|noblesvillein.name: Deer Creek Amphitheater
deercreekamphitheater|noblesvillein.extract: The Ruoff Music Center is an outdoor amphitheatre located in Noblesville, Indiana, United States. It was originally named Deer Creek Music Center and subsequently Verizon Wireless Music Center, Klipsch Music Center, and Ruoff Home Mortgage Music Center.

denvercoliseum|denverco.name: Denver Coliseum
denvercoliseum|denverco.extract: The Denver Coliseum is an indoor arena located in Denver, Colorado. The arena was built from 1949 to 1951, where the Denver Pacific Railway broke ground on its Cheyenne line in 1868.

deutschesmuseumhalle|munichwestgermany.name: Deutsches Museum Halle
deutschesmuseumhalle|munichwestgermany.extract: The Kunstmuseum Moritzburg Halle (Saale) is the art museum of the state of Saxony-Anhalt in the Moritzburg in Halle (Saale), Germany. It emerged from Städtisches Museum für Kunst und Kunstgewerbe der Stadt Halle (Saale) (lit.: Municipal Museum of Arts and Crafts of the City of Halle (Saale)), founded in 1885.

dillongymprincetonuniversity|princetonnj.name: Dillon Gym, Princeton University
dillongymprincetonuniversity|princetonnj.extract: The Princeton–Rutgers rivalry is a college rivalry in athletics between the Tigers of Princeton University and Scarlet Knights of Rutgers University – New Brunswick, both of which are located in New Jersey. The rivalry dates back to the first college football game in history in 1869, and even events prior to the first football game, having played baseball and rowed crew against each other prior to the first football game, along with engaging in the Rutgers–Princeton Cannon War.

dillonstadium|hartfordct.name: Dillon Stadium
dillonstadium|hartfordct.extract: Trinity Health Stadium (formerly Dillon Stadium) is a multipurpose facility in Hartford, Connecticut, United States. It has been host to concerts and sporting events.

electriccircus|newyorkcityny.name: Electric Circus
electriccircus|newyorkcityny.extract: The Hyatt Grand Central New York is a hotel located at 109 East 42nd Street, adjoining Grand Central Terminal, in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City. It operated as the 2,000-room Commodore Hotel between 1919 and 1976, before hotel chain Hyatt and real estate developer Donald Trump converted the hotel to the 1,400-room Grand Hyatt New York between 1978 and 1980.

empirepool|wembleyengland.name: Empire Pool
empirepool|wembleyengland.extract: Wembley Arena () (originally the Empire Pool, currently known as OVO Arena Wembley for sponsorship reasons) is an indoor arena next to Wembley Stadium in Wembley,  Greater London, England.  The 12,500-seat facility is Greater London's second-largest indoor arena after the O2 Arena, and the ninth-largest in the United Kingdom.

expositioncenter|milwaukeewi.name: Exposition Center
expositioncenter|milwaukeewi.extract: The UW–Milwaukee Panther Arena (originally the Milwaukee Arena and formerly MECCA Arena and U.S. Cellular Arena) is an indoor arena located in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The arena, which seats as many as 12,700 people and offers 41,700 square feet (3,874 m2) of floor space, is part of a larger downtown campus, that includes the Milwaukee Theatre and Wisconsin Center.
formerNames: MECCA (The Milwaukee Exposition, Convention Center and Arena) (1974–1995)

fairgroundsarena|oklahomacityok.name: Fairgrounds Arena
fairgroundsarena|oklahomacityok.extract: Jim Norick Arena (formerly Fairgrounds Arena) was a large multi-purpose arena located at State Fair Park in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Completed in 1965 at a cost of $2.4 million, it was the largest indoor facility in Oklahoma City until the construction of the Myriad Convention Center.

festhalle|frankfurtgermany.name: Fest Halle
festhalle|frankfurtgermany.extract: The Frankfurt–Göttingen railway is a continuously double track and electrified main line in Hesse and southern Lower Saxony, Germany. The line was initially built from Bebra towards Fulda by the Kurhessen State Railway.

fillmoreauditorium|sanfranciscoca.name: Fillmore Auditorium
fillmoreauditorium|sanfranciscoca.extract:
The Fillmore is a historic music venue in San Francisco, California.
Built in 1912 and originally named the Majestic Hall, it became the Fillmore Auditorium in 1954.

fillmoreeast|newyorkcityny.name: Fillmore East
fillmoreeast|newyorkcityny.extract: The Fillmore East was a rock music venue on Second Avenue near 6th Street in the East Village of Manhattan in New York City. In operation between March 8, 1968, and June 27, 1971, it belonged to then-top rock promoter Bill Graham, and featured some of the biggest acts of that time.

fillmorewest|sanfranciscoca.name: Fillmore West
fillmorewest|sanfranciscoca.extract: The Fillmore West was a historic live rock and roll music venue in San Francisco, California, US, which became famous under the direction of concert promoter Bill Graham from 1968 to 1971. Named after The Fillmore at the intersection of Fillmore Street and Geary Boulevard (which was Graham's principal venue from 1966 to 1968), it stood at the southwest corner of Market Street and South Van Ness Avenue in the Civic Center district.

forumtheater|copenhagendenmark.extract: Forum or The Forum may refer to:

foxborostadium|foxboroma.name: Foxboro Stadium
foxborostadium|foxboroma.extract: Foxboro Stadium, originally Schaefer Stadium and later Sullivan Stadium, was an outdoor stadium in the New England region of the United States, located in Foxborough, Massachusetts. It opened in 1971 and served as the home of the New England Patriots of the National Football League (NFL) for 31 seasons (through January 2002) and also as the first home venue for the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer (MLS) from 1996 to 2002.

giantsstadium|eastrutherfordnj.name: Giants Stadium
giantsstadium|eastrutherfordnj.extract: Giants Stadium (sometimes referred to as Giants Stadium at the Meadowlands) was a stadium located in East Rutherford, New Jersey, in the Meadowlands Sports Complex. The venue was open from 1976 to 2010, and primarily hosted sporting events and concerts.

glenhelenregionalpark|devoreca.name: Glen Helen Regional Park
glenhelenregionalpark|devoreca.extract: Glen Helen Regional Park is a county park located in San Bernardino, California, United States adjacent to the Cajon Pass. It was the site of both US Festivals of the early 1980s.

goldengatestudios|sanfranciscoca.name: Golden Gate Studios
goldengatestudios|sanfranciscoca.extract: Golden Gate Park is an urban park between the Richmond and Sunset districts on the West Side of San Francisco, California, United States. It is the largest urban park in the city, containing 1,017 acres (412 ha), and the third-most visited urban park in the United States, with an estimated 24 million visitors annually.

goldenhallcommunityconcourse|sandiegoca.name: Golden Hall Community Concourse
goldenhallcommunityconcourse|sandiegoca.extract: Downtown San Diego is the central business district of San Diego, California, the eighth largest city in the United States. It houses the major local headquarters of the city, county, state, and federal governments.

grandeballroom|detroitmi.name: Grande Ballroom
grandeballroom|detroitmi.extract: The Grande Ballroom  ( GRAND-ee) is a historic live music venue located at 8952 Grand River Avenue in the Petosky-Otsego neighborhood of Detroit, Michigan. The building was designed by Detroit engineer and architect Charles N. Agree in 1928 and originally served as a multi-purpose building, hosting retail business on the first floor and a large dance hall upstairs.

grandprixracecourse|watkinsglenny.name: Grand Prix Racecourse
grandprixracecourse|watkinsglenny.extract: Watkins Glen International, nicknamed "The Glen", is an automobile race track located in Dix, New York, United States, just southwest of the village of Watkins Glen for which it is named, at the southern tip of Seneca Lake. It is the former home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix, which it hosted for twenty consecutive years from 1961 to 1980.

greatwesternforum|inglewoodca.name: Great Western Forum
greatwesternforum|inglewoodca.extract: The Kia Forum, also known simply as The Forum, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Inglewood, California, part of the Los Angeles area. Located on  West Manchester Boulevard, with Pincay Drive to the south and between  Kareem Court and Prairie Avenue to the east and west, it is north of SoFi Stadium, Intuit Dome, and the Hollywood Park Casino, and about 3 miles (4.8 km) east of Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

greektheateruniversityofcalifornia|berke.name: Greek Theater, University Of California
greektheateruniversityofcalifornia|berke.extract:
The William Randolph Hearst Greek Theatre, known locally as simply the Greek Theatre, is an 8,500-seat Greek Theatre owned and operated by the University of California, Berkeley in Berkeley, California, United States.
The Greek Theatre hosts The Berkeley Jazz Festival, pop, rock, and world music concerts, UC Berkeley graduation ceremonies, occasional addresses by noted speakers, and other events.

grugahalle|essengermany.name: Gruga Halle
grugahalle|essengermany.extract: The Messe Essen is the exhibition centre of the city of Essen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is located in the Rüttenscheid borough near the Grugapark.

gulfstreamparkracetrack|hallandalefl.name: Gulfstream Park Racetrack
gulfstreamparkracetrack|hallandalefl.extract: Gulfstream Park  is a Thoroughbred horse race track, casino and outdoor entertainment and shopping destination in Hallandale Beach, Florida, United States. It is among the most important venues for horse racing in the United States, and is open 365 days a year.

hamptoncoliseum|hamptonva.name: Hampton Coliseum
hamptoncoliseum|hamptonva.extract: Hampton Coliseum is a multi-purpose arena in Hampton, Virginia. Construction began on May 24, 1968.

haraarena|daytonoh.name: Hara Arena
haraarena|daytonoh.extract: Hara Arena was a 5,500-seat multi-purpose arena located largely in the Trotwood, Ohio suburb of Dayton and partly in the Harrison Township suburb. The facility began as a ballroom in 1957, added an arena in 1964 and grew to a six-building complex which closed in August 2016.

hardingtheater|sanfranciscoca.name: Harding Theater
hardingtheater|sanfranciscoca.extract: The Harding Theater is a historic movie theater located at 616 Divisadero Street in San Francisco, California, completed in 1926, and closed c. 2004.

henryjkaiserconventioncenter|oaklandca.name: Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center
henryjkaiserconventioncenter|oaklandca.extract: The Henry J. Kaiser Center for the Arts is a historic, publicly owned multi-purpose building located in Oakland, California. Originally known as the Oakland Civic Auditorium, it was renamed in honor of Henry J. Kaiser following a 1984 renovation, and was renamed as the Henry J. Kaiser Center for the Arts in 2023.

hollederstadium|rochesterny.name: Holleder Stadium

hollederstadium|rochesterny.extract: Rochester, New York in the United States, and its suburbs, is or has been home to many famous individuals. They include businessmen, civil rights activists, politicians, entertainers, educators, and athletes.

hollywoodbowl|hollywoodca.name: Hollywood Bowl
hollywoodbowl|hollywoodca.extract: The Hollywood Bowl is an amphitheatre and public park in the Hollywood Hills of Los Angeles, California. It was named one of the ten best live music venues in the United States by Rolling Stone magazine in 2018 and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2023.

honolulucivicauditorium|honoluluhi.name: Honolulu Civic Auditorium
honolulucivicauditorium|honoluluhi.extract: The Long Beach Chiefs were an American basketball team based in Honolulu, Hawaii (1961–62) and Long Beach, California (1962–63) that was a member of the American Basketball League.

internationalamphitheater|chicagoil.name: International Amphitheater
internationalamphitheater|chicagoil.extract: The Petrillo Music Shell (sometimes referred to as the Petrillo Bandshell or formally as the James C. Petrillo Music Shell) is an outdoor amphitheater in Grant Park in the Loop community area of Chicago in Cook County, Illinois, United States.  It serves as host to many large annual music festivals in the city such as Chicago Blues Festival, Chicago Jazz Festival, Taste of Chicago and Lollapalooza.

irvinemeadowsampitheatre|irvineca.name: Irvine Meadows Ampitheatre
irvinemeadowsampitheatre|irvineca.extract: Irvine Meadows Amphitheatre (later known as Verizon Wireless Amphitheater) was an amphitheater operating from 1981 to 2016 in Irvine, California.

jahrhunderthalle|frankfurtwestgermany.name: Jahrhundert Halle
jahrhunderthalle|frankfurtwestgermany.extract: Halle (Saale), or simply Halle (German pronunciation: [ˈhalə] ), is the second largest city of the German state of Saxony-Anhalt. It is the sixth-most populous city in the area of former East Germany after (East) Berlin, Leipzig, Dresden, Chemnitz, and Magdeburg, and is Germany's 31st-largest city.

johnfkennedystadium|philadelphiapa.name: John F. Kennedy Stadium
johnfkennedystadium|philadelphiapa.extract: John F. Kennedy Stadium, formerly Philadelphia Municipal Stadium and Sesquicentennial Stadium, was an open-air stadium in Philadelphia that stood from 1926 to 1992. It was built of concrete, stone, and brick on a 13.5-acre (55,000 m2) tract in South Philadelphia.

kezarstadium|sanfranciscoca.name: Kezar Stadium
kezarstadium|sanfranciscoca.extract: Kezar Stadium () is an outdoor athletics stadium in San Francisco, California, United States, located adjacent to Kezar Pavilion in the southeastern corner of Golden Gate Park. It serves as the home of San Francisco City FC of USL League Two.

kingswoodmusictheater|torontocanada.name: Kingswood Music Theater
kingswoodmusictheater|torontocanada.extract: Kingswood Music Theatre was a 15,000-seat amphitheatre located at Canada's Wonderland in Vaughan, Ontario. Kingswood was open from May to September.

kleinhansmusichall|buffalony.name: Kleinhans Music Hall
kleinhansmusichall|buffalony.extract: Kleinhans Music Hall is a concert hall located on Symphony Circle in Buffalo, New York, United States. Designed by Eliel Saarinen and his son Eero Saarinen, Kleinhans opened on October 19, 1940 and serves as home to the Buffalo Philharmonic Orchestra, a regular venue for the Buffalo Chamber Music Society.

kqedstudios|sanfranciscoca.name: KQED Studios
kqedstudios|sanfranciscoca.extract: KQED-FM (88.5 MHz) is a noncommercial educational radio station licensed to San Francisco, California, United States, that is the primary National Public Radio (NPR) member station for the San Francisco Bay Area. It is simulcast on KQEI-FM (89.3 FM), licensed to North Highlands, California, United States, and serving the Sacramento metropolitan area.

lagunasecaraceway|montereyca.name: Laguna Seca Raceway
lagunasecaraceway|montereyca.extract: Laguna Seca Raceway (branded as WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca, and previously Mazda Raceway Laguna Seca for sponsorship reasons) is a paved road racing track near both Salinas and Monterey, California, United States. It was built in 1957 and is used for both auto racing and motorcycle racing.

lamemorialcoliseum|losangelesca.name: L.A. Memorial Coliseum
lamemorialcoliseum|losangelesca.extract: The Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum (also known as the Los Angeles Coliseum or L.A. Coliseum) is a multi-purpose stadium in the Exposition Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, United States. The Coliseum was commissioned in 1921 and completed in 1923 as a memorial to Los Angeles veterans of World War I. The stadium currently serves as the home of the University of Southern California Trojans football team, and is located directly adjacent to the school's main University Park campus.

lindleymeadowsgoldengatepark|sanfrancisc.name: Lindley Meadows, Golden Gate Park
lindleymeadowsgoldengatepark|sanfrancisc.extract: Golden Gate Park is an urban park between the Richmond and Sunset districts on the West Side of San Francisco, California, United States. It is the largest urban park in the city, containing 1,017 acres (412 ha), and the third-most visited urban park in the United States, with an estimated 24 million visitors annually.

losangelessportsarena|losangelesca.name: Los Angeles Sports Arena
losangelessportsarena|losangelesca.wikiTitle: History of the NFL in Los Angeles
losangelessportsarena|losangelesca.extract: The National Football League (NFL) has had a long and complicated history in Los Angeles, the second-largest media market in the United States, behind only New York City. Los Angeles became the first city on the West Coast to host an NFL team when the Cleveland Rams moved to Los Angeles in 1946; they played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum from 1946 until 1979.
losangelessportsarena|losangelesca.currentName: History of the NFL in Los Angeles

madisonsquaregarden|newyorkcityny.name: Madison Square Garden
madisonsquaregarden|newyorkcityny.extract: Madison Square Garden, colloquially known as the Garden or by its initials MSG, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, U.S. The arena is located between Seventh and Eighth avenues, extending from 31st to 33rd streets, atop Pennsylvania Station. The current site hosts the fourth venue to bear the name "Madison Square Garden"; the first two, opened in 1879 and 1890, were situated in Madison Square, on East 26th Street and Madison Avenue, with the third Madison Square Garden (1925) farther uptown at Eighth Avenue and 50th Street.

marincountyveteransauditorium|sanrafaelc.name: Marin County Veteran's Auditorium
marincountyveteransauditorium|sanrafaelc.extract: The Marin County Civic Center is a governmental complex in San Rafael, the county seat of Marin County, California, United States. Designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and Taliesin Associated Architects (TAA), the 140-acre (57 ha) complex consists of several buildings constructed between 1960 and 1976.

marketsquarearena|indianapolisin.name: Market Square Arena
marketsquarearena|indianapolisin.extract: Market Square Arena (MSA) was an indoor arena in Indianapolis. Completed in 1974, at a cost of $23 million, it seated 16,530 for basketball and 15,993 for ice hockey.

masonictemple|detroitmi.name: Masonic Temple
masonictemple|detroitmi.extract: The Detroit Masonic Temple is the world's largest Masonic Temple. Located in the Cass Corridor neighborhood of Detroit, Michigan, at 500 Temple Street, the building serves as a home to various masonic organizations including the York Rite Sovereign College of North America.

maxyasgursfarm|bethelny.name: Max Yasgur's Farm
maxyasgursfarm|bethelny.extract: The Woodstock Music and Art Fair, commonly referred to as Woodstock, was a music festival held from August 15 to 18, 1969, on Max Yasgur's dairy farm in Bethel, New York, 60 miles (95 km) southwest of the town of Woodstock. Billed as "an Aquarian Exposition: 3 Days of Peace & Music", it attracted an audience of more than 460,000.

mcarthurcourtuniversityoforegon|eugeneor.name: McArthur Court, University Of Oregon
mcarthurcourtuniversityoforegon|eugeneor.extract:
McArthur Court is a basketball arena located on the campus of the University of Oregon in Eugene and the former home of the Oregon Ducks men's and women's basketball teams, replaced in 2011 by Matthew Knight Arena.
Also known as "The Pit" or "Mac Court," it was known as one of the most hostile arenas in the nation.

mcdonougharenageorgetownu|washingtondc.name: McDonough Arena, Georgetown U.
mcdonougharenageorgetownu|washingtondc.extract:
McDonough Memorial Gymnasium, sometimes referred to as McDonough Arena when hosting a sports or entertainment event, is a multi-purpose arena on the campus of Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. The gymnasium opened in 1951 and can hold 2,200 spectators for sports events.
One source claims that "McDonough Gymnasium" refers to the building as a whole, while "McDonough Arena" refers only to the event space within the building where athletic and social events take place.

mcgawmemorialhall|evanstonil.name: McGaw Memorial Hall
mcgawmemorialhall|evanstonil.extract: Welsh–Ryan Arena is a multi-purpose arena in Evanston, Illinois, United States, near the campus of Northwestern University. It is home to four Northwestern Wildcats athletic teams: men's basketball, women's basketball, volleyball, and wrestling.

mcnicholssportsarena|denverco.name: McNichols Sports Arena
mcnicholssportsarena|denverco.extract: The Denver Coliseum is an indoor arena located in Denver, Colorado. The arena was built from 1949 to 1951, where the Denver Pacific Railway broke ground on its Cheyenne line in 1868.

meadowlandsarena|eastrutherfordnj.name: Meadowlands Arena
meadowlandsarena|eastrutherfordnj.extract: The Meadowlands Sports Complex is a sports complex located in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States. The facility is owned and operated by the New Jersey Sports and Exposition Authority (NJSEA).

memorialauditorium|dallastx.name: Memorial Auditorium
memorialauditorium|dallastx.extract: The Hall of State (originally the State of Texas Building) is a building in Dallas's Fair Park that commemorates the history of the U.S. state of Texas and is considered one of the best examples of Art Deco architecture in the state.  It was designed and built for the Texas Centennial Exposition.

merriweatherpostpavilion|columbiamd.name: Merriweather Post Pavilion
merriweatherpostpavilion|columbiamd.extract: Merriweather Post Pavilion is an outdoor concert venue located in the planned community of Columbia, Maryland, a suburb of Baltimore and Washington, DC. In 2010, Merriweather was named the second best amphitheater in the United States by Billboard magazine. The venue was also ranked as the fourth best amphitheater in the United States by Rolling Stone in 2013.

milehighstadium|denverco.name: Mile High Stadium
milehighstadium|denverco.extract:
Mile High Stadium (originally Bears Stadium until 1968) was an outdoor multi-purpose stadium located in Denver, Colorado, from 1948 to 2002.
The stadium was built in 1948 to accommodate the Denver Bears baseball team, which was a member of the Western League during its construction.

milwaukeeauditorium|milwaukeewi.name: Milwaukee Auditorium
milwaukeeauditorium|milwaukeewi.extract: The Milwaukee Art Museum (also referred to as MAM) is an art museum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Its collection of nearly 35,000 works of art and gallery spaces totaling 150,000 sq.

milwaukeeperformingartscenter|milwaukeew.name: Milwaukee Performing Arts Center
milwaukeeperformingartscenter|milwaukeew.extract: The Marcus Performing Arts Center is a performing arts center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, United States. Managed by a non-profit organization, it is marketed as Milwaukee's premier presenter of the performing arts.

mississippiriverfestival|edwardsvilleil.name: Mississippi River Festival
mississippiriverfestival|edwardsvilleil.extract: The Mississippi River Festival (MRF) is a summer outdoor concert series held during the years 1969-1980, and rebooted in 2024. Originally on the campus of Southern Illinois University in Edwardsville, Illinois.

montereyperformingartscenter|montereyca.name: Monterey Performing Arts Center
montereyperformingartscenter|montereyca.extract: The Monterey Museum of Art (MMA) an art museum located in Monterey, California. It was founded in 1959 [1] as a chapter of the American Federation of Arts.

nashvillemunicipalauditorium|nashvilletn.name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
nashvillemunicipalauditorium|nashvilletn.extract: The Nashville Municipal Auditorium is an indoor sports and concert venue in Nashville, Tennessee. It opened October 7, 1962 with both an arena and exhibition hall.

nassaucoliseum|uniondaleny.name: Nassau Coliseum
nassaucoliseum|uniondaleny.extract: Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum (or simply the Nassau Coliseum) is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Uniondale, New York, on Long Island. The venue is situated approximately 7 miles (11 km) east of the eastern limits of the borough of Queens in New York City, adjacent to the Meadowbrook Parkway.

nbcstudios|newyorkcityny.name: NBC Studios
nbcstudios|newyorkcityny.extract:
NBC Studios are located in the historic 30 Rockefeller Plaza (on Sixth Avenue between 49th and 50th streets) in Manhattan, New York City. The building houses the NBC television network headquarters, its parent NBCUniversal, and NBC's flagship station WNBC (Channel 4), as well as Telemundo's flagship station WNJU.
The first NBC Radio City Studios began operating in the early 1930s.

nevadacountyfairgrounds|grassvalleyca.name: Nevada County Fairgrounds
nevadacountyfairgrounds|grassvalleyca.extract: North Star House (alternate: Foote Mansion) is a mansion located roughly a mile south of Grass Valley, Nevada County, northern California. In 1904, James Hague, president of the North Star Mine, commissioned Julia Morgan, a newly licensed California architect, to design the 11,000 square foot building.

newcastleunderlyme|newcastleengland.name: Newcastle-Under-Lyme
newcastleunderlyme|newcastleengland.extract: Newcastle-under-Lyme is a market town and the administrative centre of the Borough of Newcastle-under-Lyme in Staffordshire, England. It is adjacent to the city of Stoke-on-Trent.

nystatepavilionflushingmeadowpark|queens.name: NY State Pavilion, Flushing Meadow Park
nystatepavilionflushingmeadowpark|queens.extract: Flushing Meadows–Corona Park (often referred to as Flushing Meadows Park or simply Flushing Meadows or Corona Park) is a public park in the northern part of Queens in New York City, New York, U.S. It is bounded by I-678 (Van Wyck Expressway) on the east, Grand Central Parkway on the west, Flushing Bay on the north, and Union Turnpike on the south. Flushing Meadows–Corona Park is the fourth-largest public park in New York City, with a total area of 897 acres (363 ha).

oaklandcoliseumarena|oaklandca.name: Oakland Coliseum Arena
oaklandcoliseumarena|oaklandca.extract:
Oakland Arena, often referred to as the Oakland Coliseum Arena, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Oakland, California, United States, and one of two venues within the Oakland–Alameda County Coliseum Complex. 
Opened in 1966, the Oakland Arena was originally the location of the California Seals of the Western Hockey League (WHL), later of the National Hockey League (NHL), until their move to Cleveland in 1976.

oaklandcoliseumstadium|oaklandca.name: Oakland Coliseum Stadium
oaklandcoliseumstadium|oaklandca.extract: The station complex of Amtrak's Oakland Coliseum station and Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART)'s Coliseum station is located in the East Oakland area of Oakland, California, United States. The two stations, located about 600 feet (180 m) apart, are connected to each other and to the Oakland Coliseum/Oakland Arena sports complex with an accessible pedestrian bridge.

okeefecenter|torontocanada.name: O'Keefe Center
okeefecenter|torontocanada.extract: Vivian Reiss (born 1952) is an artist and the owner of the Reiss Gallery in Toronto, Canada. She still spends time in New York City, but she has lived and worked in Toronto since 1975.

onondagawarmemorialauditorium|syracuseny.name: Onondaga War Memorial Auditorium
onondagawarmemorialauditorium|syracuseny.extract: The Upstate Medical University Arena (originally known as Onondaga County War Memorial and later as the Oncenter War Memorial Arena) is a multi-purpose arena located in Syracuse, New York. It is part of the Oncenter Complex.

oregoncountyfairsite|venetaor.name: Oregon County Fair Site
oregoncountyfairsite|venetaor.extract: The Oregon Country Fair (OCF) is a nonprofit organization and an annual three-day art and music fair held outside the city limits of Veneta, Oregon, United States. Located in the Willamette Valley, the site is about 13 miles (21 km) west of Eugene along the Long Tom River near the unincorporated community of Elmira.

palaisdessports|parisfrance.name: Palais Des Sports
palaisdessports|parisfrance.extract: The Dôme de Paris (French pronunciation: [dom də paʁi]; originally the Palais des Sports) is an indoor arena located in the 15th arrondissement of Paris, France. The closest metro station is Porte de Versailles.

paramounttheater|portlandor.name: Paramount Theater
paramounttheater|portlandor.extract: The Arlene Schnitzer Concert Hall (originally Portland Publix Theatre and Paramount Theatre) is a historic theater building and performing arts center in Portland, Oregon, United States. Part of the Portland Center for the Performing Arts, it is home to the Oregon Symphony, Portland Youth Philharmonic, Metropolitan Youth Symphony, White Bird Dance Company, and Portland Arts & Lectures.

paramounttheatre|portlandor.name: Paramount Theatre
paramounttheatre|portlandor.extract: The Arlene Schnitzer Concert Hall (originally Portland Publix Theatre and Paramount Theatre) is a historic theater building and performing arts center in Portland, Oregon, United States. Part of the Portland Center for the Performing Arts, it is home to the Oregon Symphony, Portland Youth Philharmonic, Metropolitan Youth Symphony, White Bird Dance Company, and Portland Arts & Lectures.

parkwestskiresort|saltlakecityut.name: Park West Ski Resort
parkwestskiresort|saltlakecityut.extract: Park City Mountain Resort (PCMR) is a ski resort in the western United States in Park City, Utah, located 32 miles (51 km) east of Salt Lake City. Park City, as the ski resort and area is known, contains several training courses for the U.S. Ski Team, including slalom and giant slalom runs.

pauleyballroomuofcalifornia|berkeleyca.name: Pauley Ballroom, U. Of California
pauleyballroomuofcalifornia|berkeleyca.extract:
The William Randolph Hearst Greek Theatre, known locally as simply the Greek Theatre, is an 8,500-seat Greek Theatre owned and operated by the University of California, Berkeley in Berkeley, California, United States.
The Greek Theatre hosts The Berkeley Jazz Festival, pop, rock, and world music concerts, UC Berkeley graduation ceremonies, occasional addresses by noted speakers, and other events.

pershingmunicipalauditorium|lincolnne.name: Pershing Municipal Auditorium
pershingmunicipalauditorium|lincolnne.extract: The Pershing Center (originally known as Pershing Auditorium) was a 4,526-seat multi-purpose arena in Lincoln, Nebraska, United States. The arena opened on March 10, 1957 and was named after General John J. Pershing.

pineknobmusictheater|clarkstonmi.name: Pine Knob Music Theater
pineknobmusictheater|clarkstonmi.extract: Pine Knob Music Theatre (formerly DTE Energy Music Theatre) is an outdoor amphitheater located in Independence Township, Michigan, approximately 40 miles (64 km) northwest of Detroit. Built by the Nederlander Organization in the early 1970s, it is known as "Pine Knob Music Theatre" due to its proximity to the nearby Pine Knob ski area and golf course.

pittsburghcivicarena|pittsburghpa.name: Pittsburgh Civic Arena
pittsburghcivicarena|pittsburghpa.extract: The Civic Arena, formerly the Civic Auditorium and later Mellon Arena, was a multi-purpose arena located in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It primarily served as the home to the Pittsburgh Penguins, the city's National Hockey League (NHL) franchise, from 1967 to 2010.

placevillemarie|montrealcanada.name: Place Ville Marie
placevillemarie|montrealcanada.extract: Place Ville Marie (French pronunciation: [plas vil maʁi], abbr. PVM) is a large office and shopping complex skyscraper in Downtown Montreal, Quebec, Canada, comprising four office buildings and an underground shopping plaza.

playboyafterdark|newyorkcityny.name: Playboy After Dark
playboyafterdark|newyorkcityny.wikiTitle: List of songs about New York City
playboyafterdark|newyorkcityny.extract: Many songs are set in New York City or named after a location or feature of the city, beyond simply "name-checking" New York along with other cities.
playboyafterdark|newyorkcityny.currentName: List of songs about New York City

playhousetheater|edinburghscotland.name: Playhouse Theater
playhousetheater|edinburghscotland.extract: Playhouse (German: Schauspielhaus) is a common term for a theatre.

pnecoliseum|vancouvercanada.name: P.N.E. Coliseum
pnecoliseum|vancouvercanada.extract: Pacific Coliseum, locally known as The Coliseum or the Rink on Renfrew, is an indoor arena located at Hastings Park in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Its main use has been for ice hockey and the arena has been the home for several ice hockey teams.

pnegardenauditorium|vancouverbccanada.name: P.N.E. Garden Auditorium
pnegardenauditorium|vancouverbccanada.extract: PNE Garden Auditorium is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Vancouver, Canada, located on the grounds of the Pacific National Exhibition. It opened in 1940 and was known as the Exhibition Garden.

polofieldgoldengatepark|sanfranciscoca.name: Polo Field, Golden Gate Park
polofieldgoldengatepark|sanfranciscoca.extract: Golden Gate Park is an urban park between the Richmond and Sunset districts on the West Side of San Francisco, California, United States. It is the largest urban park in the city, containing 1,017 acres (412 ha), and the third-most visited urban park in the United States, with an estimated 24 million visitors annually.

poplarcreekpavilion|poplarcreekil.name: Poplar Creek Pavilion
poplarcreekpavilion|poplarcreekil.extract: Poplar Creek Music Theater was a concert amphitheatre in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. It opened in 1980 and closed in 1994.

portlandinternationalspeedway|portlandor.name: Portland International Speedway
portlandinternationalspeedway|portlandor.extract: Portland International Raceway (PIR) is a motorsport facility located in Portland, Oregon, United States. It is part of the Delta Park complex on the former site of Vanport, just south of the Columbia River.

portlandmeadows|portlandor.name: Portland Meadows
portlandmeadows|portlandor.extract: Portland Meadows was an American horse racing venue in Portland, Oregon, owned by The Stronach Group since July 3, 2011 and previously owned by MI Developments Inc. (MID) 2001.

portlandmemorialcoliseum|portlandor.name: Portland Memorial Coliseum
portlandmemorialcoliseum|portlandor.extract: The Veterans Memorial Coliseum (originally known as the Memorial Coliseum) is an indoor arena located in the oldest part of the Rose Quarter area in Portland, Oregon. The arena is the home of the Portland Winterhawks, a major junior ice hockey team, and was the original home of the Portland Trail Blazers of the National Basketball Association.

providenceciviccenter|providenceri.name: Providence Civic Center
providenceciviccenter|providenceri.extract: The Amica Mutual Pavilion (originally Providence Civic Center and formerly Dunkin' Donuts Center ("The Dunk")) is an indoor arena located in downtown Providence, Rhode Island. It was built in 1972, as a home court for the Providence College Friars men's basketball program, due to the high demand for tickets to their games in Alumni Hall, as well as for a home arena for the then–Providence Reds, who played in the nearly 50-year-old Rhode Island Auditorium.

racewaypark|englishtownnj.name: Raceway Park
racewaypark|englishtownnj.extract: Old Bridge Township Raceway Park, originally known as Madison Township Raceway Park, is an American auto racing facility located in Old Bridge Township, in Middlesex County, New Jersey, United States (with an Englishtown ZIP code).

radio|luxembourgluxembourg.name: Radio
radio|luxembourgluxembourg.extract: Luxembourg has a developed economy largely dependent on the banking, steel, and industrial sectors. Citizens of Luxembourg enjoy the highest per capita gross domestic product in the world, according to an IMF estimate in 2022.

radiocitymusichall|newyorkcityny.name: Radio City Music Hall
radiocitymusichall|newyorkcityny.extract: Radio City Music Hall (also known as Radio City) is an entertainment venue and theater at 1260 Avenue of the Americas, within Rockefeller Center, in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City. Nicknamed "The Showplace of the Nation", it is the headquarters for the Rockettes.

recreationhallucdavis|davisca.name: Recreation Hall (UC Davis)
recreationhallucdavis|davisca.extract: The University Credit Union Center (previously known as Recreation Hall and The Pavilion at the ARC and commonly known as The Pavilion) is a 7,600-seat indoor multi-purpose stadium on the campus of the University of California, Davis in unincorporated Yolo County, California.

redrocksamphitheater|morrisonco.name: Red Rocks Amphitheater
redrocksamphitheater|morrisonco.extract: Red Rocks Amphitheatre (also known colloquially as Red Rocks) is an open-air amphitheater near Morrison, Colorado, approximately ten miles (16 km) southwest of Denver. It is owned and operated by the city of  Denver.

renocentennialcoliseum|renonv.name: Reno Centennial Coliseum
renocentennialcoliseum|renonv.extract: The Reno-Sparks Convention Center is a convention center in the western United States, located in Reno, Nevada. Opened 61 years ago in 1965 as Centennial Coliseum, it hosted the Big Sky Conference basketball tournament in 1983, and also hosts boxing matches.

reunionarena|dallastx.name: Reunion Arena
reunionarena|dallastx.extract: Reunion Arena was a multi-purpose indoor arena located in the Reunion district of downtown Dallas, Texas, United States. The arena served as the primary home of the National Hockey League's (NHL) Dallas Stars and the National Basketball Association's (NBA) Dallas Mavericks.

rhodeislandauditorium|providenceri.name: Rhode Island Auditorium
rhodeislandauditorium|providenceri.extract: Rhode Island Auditorium was an indoor arena in Providence, Rhode Island, at 1111 North Main Street. It hosted the BAA's Providence Steamrollers from 1946 until 1949, and the Providence Reds ice hockey team until the Providence Civic Center (now the Amica Mutual Pavilion) was opened in 1972.

richmondcoliseum|richmondva.name: Richmond Coliseum
richmondcoliseum|richmondva.extract: Richmond Coliseum is a defunct arena located in downtown Richmond, Virginia, with a capacity of 13,500 that was most often used for various large concerts. The arena opened in 1971 and the region is looking to replace the aging facility with a larger one.

richstadium|buffalony.name: Rich Stadium
richstadium|buffalony.extract: Ralph Wilson Stadium, colloquially known as The Ralph, was a stadium in Orchard Park, New York, in the Southtowns of the Buffalo metropolitan area. It served as the home venue of the Buffalo Bills of the National Football League (NFL) from 1973 to 2025.

riverbendmusiccenter|cincinnatioh.name: River Bend Music Center
riverbendmusiccenter|cincinnatioh.extract: Cincinnati began with the settlement of Columbia, Losantiville, and North Bend in the Northwest Territory of the United States beginning in late December 1788. The following year Fort Washington, named for George Washington, was established to protect the settlers.

riverfrontarena|cincinnatioh.name: Riverfront Arena
riverfrontarena|cincinnatioh.extract: Heritage Bank Center is an indoor arena in downtown Cincinnati, adjacent to Great American Ball Park. It was completed in September 1975 and named Riverfront Coliseum because of its placement next to Riverfront Stadium.

riverfrontcoliseum|cincinnatioh.name: River Front Coliseum
riverfrontcoliseum|cincinnatioh.extract: Heritage Bank Center is an indoor arena in downtown Cincinnati, adjacent to Great American Ball Park. It was completed in September 1975 and named Riverfront Coliseum because of its placement next to Riverfront Stadium.

riverportamphitheatre|marylandheightsmo.name: Riverport Amphitheatre
riverportamphitheatre|marylandheightsmo.extract: Hollywood Casino Amphitheater (originally Riverport Amphitheatre and formerly the UMB Bank Pavilion and Verizon Wireless Amphitheater) is an outdoor concert venue in Maryland Heights, Missouri, near St. Louis.

robertfkennedystadium|washingtondcdc.name: Robert F. Kennedy Stadium
robertfkennedystadium|washingtondcdc.extract: Robert F. Kennedy Memorial Stadium, commonly known as RFK Stadium and originally known as District of Columbia Stadium, was a multi-purpose stadium in Washington, D.C. It was located along the Anacostia River on East Capitol Street in the city's Hill East neighborhood. The stadium was in operation from 1961 to 2019, with it being deconstructed and to be replaced with the New Stadium at RFK Campus by 2030.

rooseveltstadium|jerseycitynj.name: Roosevelt Stadium
rooseveltstadium|jerseycitynj.extract: Roosevelt Stadium was a baseball stadium at Droyer's Point in Jersey City, New Jersey. It opened on April 23, 1937, and was the home of the Jersey City Giants of the International League (IL), the Triple-A farm team of the New York Giants, from 1937 to 1950 and later hosted other high-minor league baseball teams.

rubberbowl|akronoh.name: Rubber Bowl
rubberbowl|akronoh.extract: The Rubber Bowl was a stadium located in Akron, Ohio, that was primarily used for American football.  From its opening in 1940 until 2008, it served as the home field of the Akron Zips football team of the University of Akron prior to the opening of InfoCision Stadium–Summa Field.

saengerperformingartscenter|neworleansla.name: Saenger Performing Arts Center
saengerperformingartscenter|neworleansla.wikiTitle: Mahalia Jackson Theater of the Performing Arts
saengerperformingartscenter|neworleansla.extract: The Mahalia Jackson Theater of the Performing Arts is a theater located in Louis Armstrong Park in New Orleans, Louisiana. It was named after gospel singer Mahalia Jackson, who was born in New Orleans.

santaclaracountyfairgrounds|sanjoseca.name: Santa Clara County Fairgrounds
santaclaracountyfairgrounds|sanjoseca.wikiTitle: California county routes in zone G
santaclaracountyfairgrounds|sanjoseca.extract: There are 21 routes assigned to the "G" zone of the California Route Marker Program, which designates county routes in California. The "G" zone includes county highways in Monterey, San Benito, San Luis Obispo, Santa Clara, and Santa Cruz counties.
santaclaracountyfairgrounds|sanjoseca.currentName: California county routes in zone G

saratogaperformingartscenter|saratogaspr.name: Saratoga Performing Arts Center
saratogaperformingartscenter|saratogaspr.extract: Saratoga Performing Arts Center (SPAC), also known as Albany Med Health System at SPAC for Live Nation-promoted events, is a large amphitheatre located in Saratoga Springs, New York, on the grounds of Saratoga Spa State Park. It presents summer performances of classical music, jazz, pop and rock, country, comedy, and dance.

saturdaynightlivenbcstudios|newyorkcityn.name: Saturday Night Live, NBC Studios
saturdaynightlivenbcstudios|newyorkcityn.extract:
NBC Studios are located in the historic 30 Rockefeller Plaza (on Sixth Avenue between 49th and 50th streets) in Manhattan, New York City. The building houses the NBC television network headquarters, its parent NBCUniversal, and NBC's flagship station WNBC (Channel 4), as well as Telemundo's flagship station WNJU.
The first NBC Radio City Studios began operating in the early 1930s.

sellandarena|fresnoca.name: Selland Arena
sellandarena|fresnoca.extract: Selland Arena is a multi-purpose arena built in 1966 that makes up part of a four-venue complex of the Fresno Convention and Entertainment Center in Fresno, California. It is named after former Fresno mayor Arthur L. Selland and has had over 10 million people walk through its doors in its over 50-year history.

shorelineamphitheatre|mountainviewca.name: Shoreline Amphitheatre
shorelineamphitheatre|mountainviewca.extract: Shoreline Amphitheatre is an outdoor amphitheater located in Mountain View, California, in the San Francisco Bay Area. The venue has a capacity of 22,500, with 6,500 reserved seats and 16,000 general admission on the lawn.

shrineauditorium|losangelesca.name: Shrine Auditorium
shrineauditorium|losangelesca.extract: The Shrine Auditorium and Expo Hall is a landmark large-event venue in Los Angeles. It is also the headquarters of the Al Malaikah Temple, a division of the Shriners.

silvahallhultcenter|eugeneor.name: Silva Hall (Hult Center)
silvahallhultcenter|eugeneor.wikiTitle: Hult Center for the Performing Arts
silvahallhultcenter|eugeneor.extract:
The Hult Center for the Performing Arts is a performing arts venue in Eugene, Oregon.
The Hult Center is located downtown on Willamette Street between 6th & 7th Avenues, adjacent to the Graduate Eugene (previously Hilton Eugene) and Conference Center.
silvahallhultcenter|eugeneor.currentName: Hult Center for the Performing Arts

silverstadium|rochesterny.name: Silver Stadium
silverstadium|rochesterny.extract: Silver Stadium was a baseball stadium located at 500 Norton Street in Rochester, New York. It was the home stadium for the Rochester Red Wings of the International League from 1929 to 1996, and for the New York Black Yankees of the Negro National League for their final season in 1948.

soldierfield|chicagoil.name: Soldier Field
soldierfield|chicagoil.extract: Soldier Field (historically often referred to as Soldiers' Field) is a multi-purpose stadium on the Near South Side of Chicago, Illinois, United States. Opened in 1924, the stadium has served as the home of the Chicago Bears of the National Football League (NFL) since 1971, as well as Chicago Fire FC of Major League Soccer (MLS) since 2020.

soldiersandsailorsmemorialhall|kansascit.name: Soldiers' And Sailors' Memorial Hall
soldiersandsailorsmemorialhall|kansascit.extract: Memorial Hall, or Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Building, is a multi-purpose auditorium located in Kansas City, Kansas. The 3,500-seat auditorium, which has a permanent stage, is used for public assemblies, concerts and sporting events.

southernstaramphitheater|houstontx.name: Southern Star Amphitheater
southernstaramphitheater|houstontx.extract: Southern Star Amphitheatre  was an amphitheatre located at AstroWorld in Houston, Texas. It opened in the southeast corner of the theme park in 1985.

spartanstadium|sanjoseca.name: Spartan Stadium
spartanstadium|sanjoseca.extract: CEFCU ('sef-kyü) Stadium, formerly known as Spartan Stadium, is an outdoor athletic stadium located in the Spartan Keyes neighborhood of San Jose, California. Owned by San José State University, the venue is the longtime home of Spartan football; it also hosts the university's commencement ceremony on Memorial Day weekend, and occasional high school football games.

spokanecoliseum|spokanewa.name: Spokane Coliseum
spokanecoliseum|spokanewa.extract: Spokane, Washington has a rich sporting culture and the area residents are active in many spectator and participant sports. Although Spokane lacks any major, nationally recognized professional sports team, Spokane has a sports friendly atmosphere, and was recognized and rated #99 in the Sporting News 2006 "99 Best Sporting Cities" list.

stanleytheater|pittsburghpa.name: Stanley Theater
stanleytheater|pittsburghpa.extract: The Benedum Center for the Performing Arts (formerly the Stanley Theatre) is a theater and concert hall located at 237 7th Street in the Cultural District of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.  Designed by the Philadelphia architectural firm Hoffman-Henon, it was built in 1928 as the Stanley Theatre.

starlakeamphitheater|burgettstownpa.name: Star Lake Amphitheater
starlakeamphitheater|burgettstownpa.extract: The Pavilion at Star Lake, originally Coca-Cola Star Lake Amphitheater, is an outdoor amphitheater near Burgettstown, Pennsylvania, United States, 25 miles (40 km) west of Pittsburgh. The venue holds approximately 23,000 fans: 7,100 in a reserved-seating, open-air pavilion and an additional 16,000 on a general-admission lawn.

statefaircoliseum|indianapolisin.name: State Fair Coliseum
statefaircoliseum|indianapolisin.extract: The Corteva Coliseum is a 6,500-seat indoor multi-use arena, located on the Indiana State Fairgrounds in Indianapolis. It was originally called the Indiana State Fairgrounds Coliseum and later the Pepsi Coliseum, Fairgrounds Coliseum, and Indiana Farmers Coliseum.

stlouisarena|stlouismo.name: St. Louis Arena
stlouisarena|stlouismo.extract: St. Louis Arena (known as the Checkerdome from 1977 to 1983) was an indoor arena in St.

stpaulciviccenter|stpaulmn.name: St. Paul Civic Center
stpaulciviccenter|stpaulmn.extract: The St. Paul Civic Center was an indoor arena located in Saint Paul, Minnesota.

sullivanstadium|foxboroma.name: Sullivan Stadium
sullivanstadium|foxboroma.extract: Foxboro Stadium, originally Schaefer Stadium and later Sullivan Stadium, was an outdoor stadium in the New England region of the United States, located in Foxborough, Massachusetts. It opened in 1971 and served as the home of the New England Patriots of the National Football League (NFL) for 31 seasons (through January 2002) and also as the first home venue for the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer (MLS) from 1996 to 2002.

swingauditorium|sanbernardinoca.name: Swing Auditorium
swingauditorium|sanbernardinoca.extract: The Swing Auditorium was an indoor arena located at 689 E Street in San Bernardino, California. It had a capacity of 10,000 patrons.

tacomadome|tacomawa.name: Tacoma Dome
tacomadome|tacomawa.extract: The Tacoma Dome is an indoor multi-purpose arena in Tacoma, Washington, United States. It is located south of Downtown Tacoma, adjacent to Interstate 5 and Tacoma Dome Station.

taftauditorium|cincinnatioh.name: Taft Auditorium
taftauditorium|cincinnatioh.extract: The Taft Theatre is a theater, located in Cincinnati, Ohio. The theatre was built in 1928 with an Art Deco interior.

thedeandomeuniversityofnc|chapelhillnc.name: The Dean Dome (University Of NC)
thedeandomeuniversityofnc|chapelhillnc.extract: The Dean E. Smith Student Activities Center (commonly known as the Dean Smith Center, Smith Center, or the Dean Dome) is a multi-purpose arena in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, used primarily as the home for the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Tar Heels men's basketball team. The university began to inquire about building a standalone arena for the men's basketball team beginning in the mid-1970s, but due to an ongoing university wide investigation, the fundraiser halted until its conclusion.
formerNames: Dean E. Smith Student Activities Center

thefabulousforum|inglewoodca.name: The Fabulous Forum
thefabulousforum|inglewoodca.extract: The Kia Forum, also known simply as The Forum, is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Inglewood, California, part of the Los Angeles area. Located on  West Manchester Boulevard, with Pincay Drive to the south and between  Kareem Court and Prairie Avenue to the east and west, it is north of SoFi Stadium, Intuit Dome, and the Hollywood Park Casino, and about 3 miles (4.8 km) east of Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

thehippodrome|parisfrance.name: The Hippodrome
thehippodrome|parisfrance.extract: The Hippodrome de Vincennes, also called Vincennes Racecourse, is a horse racing track located in Paris, France. It has a spectator capacity of 35,000.

theicc|berlingermany.name: The I.C.C.
theicc|berlingermany.extract: The Internationales Congress Centrum Berlin (ICC Berlin) is a former convention centre in the Westend locality of Berlin, adjacent to the Messe Berlin exhibition grounds. Designed by Ralf Schüler and Ursulina Schüler-Witte and built between 1973 and 1979, the aluminium-clad building is a major example of high-tech architecture.

thelmatheater|losangelesca.name: Thelma Theater
thelmatheater|losangelesca.extract: The Sinai Temple is a Conservative synagogue located at 10400 Wilshire Boulevard, Westwood, Los Angeles, California, in the United States. Sinai Temple is the oldest and largest Conservative congregation in the greater Los Angeles area.

themecca|milwaukeewi.name: The Mecca
themecca|milwaukeewi.extract: The UW–Milwaukee Panther Arena (originally the Milwaukee Arena and formerly MECCA Arena and U.S. Cellular Arena) is an indoor arena located in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The arena, which seats as many as 12,700 people and offers 41,700 square feet (3,874 m2) of floor space, is part of a larger downtown campus, that includes the Milwaukee Theatre and Wisconsin Center.
formerNames: MECCA (The Milwaukee Exposition, Convention Center and Arena) (1974–1995)

themosque|richmondva.name: The Mosque
themosque|richmondva.extract: The Altria Theater, sometimes referred to as "the Mosque," in Richmond, Virginia, United States is a theater at the southwest corner of Monroe Park on the campus of Virginia Commonwealth University, and is the largest venue of Richmond CenterStage's performing arts complex. Formerly known as The Mosque and the Landmark Theater, the Altria Theater was originally built for Shriners of the Acca Temple Shrine.

themusicbox|omahane.name: The Music Box
themusicbox|omahane.wikiTitle: List of theaters in Omaha, Nebraska
themusicbox|omahane.extract: This is a list of theaters in Omaha, Nebraska.  The entries include theaters used to present films and professional live performances, including vaudeville acts, plays and musical performances.
themusicbox|omahane.currentName: List of theaters in Omaha, Nebraska

theomni|atlantaga.name: The Omni
theomni|atlantaga.extract: Omni Coliseum (often called The Omni) was an indoor arena in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. Completed in 1972, the arena seated 16,378 for basketball and 15,278 for hockey.

thepalace|auburnhillsmi.name: The Palace
thepalace|auburnhillsmi.extract: The Palace of Auburn Hills, commonly known as the Palace, was a multi-purpose arena located in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Opened in 1988, it was the home of the Detroit Pistons of the National Basketball Association (NBA), the Detroit Shock of the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA), the Detroit Vipers of the International Hockey League, the Detroit Rockers of the National Professional Soccer League, the Detroit Neon/Detroit Safari of the Continental Indoor Soccer League, and the Detroit Fury of the Arena Football League.

thepalladium|newyorkcityny.name: The Palladium
thepalladium|newyorkcityny.extract: The Palladium (originally called the Academy of Music) was a movie theatre, concert hall, and finally a nightclub in New York City. It was located on the south side of East 14th Street, between Irving Place and Third Avenue.

thepyramid|memphistn.name: The Pyramid
thepyramid|memphistn.extract: The Memphis Pyramid, formerly known as the Great American Pyramid and the Pyramid Arena, and colloquially known as the Bass Pro Shops Pyramid, is a pyramid-shaped building located in downtown Memphis, Tennessee, United States, at the bank of the Mississippi River. Built in 1991 as a 20,142-seat arena, the facility was owned and operated jointly by the city of Memphis and Shelby County until Shelby County sold its share to Memphis in April 2009.

thescope|norfolkva.name: The Scope
thescope|norfolkva.extract:
Norfolk Scope is a multi-function complex in Norfolk, Virginia, comprising the 11,000-seat Scope Arena, a 2,500-seat theater known as Chrysler Hall, a 65,000-square-foot (6,000 m2) modular exhibition hall, and a 600-car parking garage.
The arena was designed by Italian architect/engineer Pier Luigi Nervi in conjunction with the (now defunct) local firm Williams and Tazewell, which designed the entire complex.

thespectrum|philadelphiapa.name: The Spectrum
thespectrum|philadelphiapa.extract: The Spectrum (later known as CoreStates Spectrum, First Union Spectrum and Wachovia Spectrum) was an indoor arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The arena opened in September 1967 as part of what is now known as the South Philadelphia Sports Complex.

thezenith|parisfrance.name: The Zenith
thezenith|parisfrance.extract: Zénith Paris (originally known as Zénith de Paris, pronounced [zenit də paʁi]; and commonly referred to as Le Zénith, [lə zenit]) is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Paris, France. It is located in the Parc de la Villette in the 19th arrondissement on the edge of the Canal de l'Ourcq.

threeriversstadium|pittsburghpa.name: Three Rivers Stadium
threeriversstadium|pittsburghpa.extract: Three Rivers Stadium was a multi-purpose stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States, from 1970 to 2000. It was home to the Pittsburgh Pirates of Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Pittsburgh Steelers of the National Football League (NFL).

tulsafairgroundspavilion|tulsaok.name: Tulsa Fairgrounds Pavilion
tulsafairgroundspavilion|tulsaok.extract:
The Expo Square Pavilion, sometimes called simply The Pavilion, and formerly known as the Tulsa Fairgrounds Pavilion, is a 6,311-seat multi-purpose arena, in the Tulsa State Fairgrounds in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
It was built in 1932; the architect was Leland I Shumway.

unganosnightclub|newyorkcityny.name: Ungano's Night Club
unganosnightclub|newyorkcityny.extract: The Concert for Bangladesh (or Bangla Desh, as the country's name was originally spelled) was a pair of benefit concerts organised by former Beatles guitarist George Harrison and the Indian sitar player Ravi Shankar. The shows were held at 2:30 and 8:00 pm on Sunday, 1 August 1971, at Madison Square Garden in New York City, to raise international awareness of, and fund relief for refugees from East Pakistan, following the Bangladesh Liberation War-related genocide and the 1970 Bhola cyclone.

universalamphitheater|universalcityca.name: Universal AmphiTheater
universalamphitheater|universalcityca.extract: Universal Amphitheatre (later known as Gibson Amphitheatre) was an indoor amphitheater located in Los Angeles, California, within Universal City. It was built as an outdoor venue, opening in the summer of 1972 with a production of Jesus Christ Superstar.

universityofvirginia|charlottesvilleva.name: University Of Virginia
universityofvirginia|charlottesvilleva.wikiTitle: Monticello and the University of Virginia in Charlottesville
universityofvirginia|charlottesvilleva.extract:
Monticello and the University of Virginia in Charlottesville is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the U.S. state of Virginia.
Thomas Jefferson (1743–1826), author of the American Declaration of Independence and third President of the United States, was also a talented architect of neoclassical buildings.
universityofvirginia|charlottesvilleva.currentName: Monticello and the University of Virginia in Charlottesville

unknownvenue|unknowncityunknownstate.name: Unknown Venue
unknownvenue|unknowncityunknownstate.extract: The Monument to the Unknown Hero (Serbian: Споменик Незнаном јунаку, romanized: Spomenik Neznanom junaku) is a Balkan Wars and World War I memorial located atop Mount Avala, south-east of Belgrade, Serbia, and designed by the sculptor Ivan Meštrović. The memorial was built in 1934–1938 on the place where an unknown Serbian World War I soldier was buried.

uptowntheater|chicagoil.name: Uptown Theater
uptowntheater|chicagoil.extract: Uptown Theatre (also known as Balaban and Katz Uptown Theatre) is a former movie palace and concert venue located in the Uptown neighborhood of Chicago, Illinois. Designed by Rapp and Rapp and built by Paschen Bros.

usairarena|landovermd.name: USAir Arena
usairarena|landovermd.extract:
The Capital Centre (later USAir Arena and US Airways Arena) was an indoor arena in the eastern United States, located in Landover, Maryland, a suburb east of Washington, D.C.  The seating capacity was 18,756 for basketball and 18,130 for hockey.
Opened in late 1973, it closed in March 2002, and was demolished that December.
formerNames: (not a former name if title of article)-->

uticamemorialauditorium|uticany.name: Utica Memorial Auditorium
uticamemorialauditorium|uticany.extract: NBT Bank Arena at the Utica Memorial Auditorium is a 3,999-seat multi-purpose arena in Utica, New York, with a capacity of 5,700 for concerts. Nicknamed the Aud, it is the home arena of the Utica Comets, the AHL affiliate of the NHL's New Jersey Devils, and Utica City FC of the Major Arena Soccer League.
formerNames: Adirondack Bank Center at the Utica Memorial Auditorium (2017–2026)

veteransmemorialcoliseum|newhavenct.name: Veterans' Memorial Coliseum
veteransmemorialcoliseum|newhavenct.extract: New Haven Coliseum, formally known as New Haven Veterans Memorial Coliseum, was a sports and entertainment arena located in downtown New Haven, Connecticut. Construction began in 1968 and was completed in 1972.

wallacewadestadiumdukeuniversity|durhamn.name: Wallace Wade Stadium, Duke University
wallacewadestadiumdukeuniversity|durhamn.extract: Wallace Wade Stadium, in full Brooks Field at Wallace Wade Stadium, is a 35,018-seat outdoor stadium in the southeastern United States, located on the campus of Duke University in Durham, North Carolina. Primarily used for American football, it is the home field of the Duke Blue Devils of the Atlantic Coast Conference.

warfieldtheater|sanfranciscoca.name: Warfield Theater
warfieldtheater|sanfranciscoca.extract: The Warfield Theatre, colloquially called The Warfield, is a 2,454 capacity event venue located in the Theatre District in downtown San Francisco, California, United States. It was built as a vaudeville theater and opened as the Loews Warfield on May 13, 1922.

warmemorialauditorium|buffalony.name: War Memorial Auditorium
warmemorialauditorium|buffalony.extract: War Memorial Stadium, colloquially known as The Rockpile, was an outdoor football, baseball and soccer stadium in Buffalo, New York. Opened in 1937 as Roesch Memorial Stadium, the venue was later known as Grover Cleveland Stadium and Civic Stadium.

warmemorialauditorium|rochesterny.name: War Memorial Auditorium
warmemorialauditorium|rochesterny.extract: Blue Cross Arena, also known as the War Memorial, is a multi-purpose indoor arena located in Rochester, New York. For hockey and lacrosse, its seating capacity is 10,662.

wembleyarena|londonengland.name: Wembley Arena
wembleyarena|londonengland.extract: Wembley Arena () (originally the Empire Pool, currently known as OVO Arena Wembley for sponsorship reasons) is an indoor arena next to Wembley Stadium in Wembley,  Greater London, England.  The 12,500-seat facility is Greater London's second-largest indoor arena after the O2 Arena, and the ninth-largest in the United Kingdom.

winterlandarena|sanfranciscoca.name: Winterland Arena
winterlandarena|sanfranciscoca.extract:
Winterland, called at first New Dreamland Auditorium and later Winterland Arena and Winterland Ballroom, was an ice-skating rink and music venue in San Francisco operational from 1928 to 1979 and demolished in 1986. 
Built at the corner of Post Street and Steiner Street, it was converted for exclusive use for music in 1971 by concert promoter Bill Graham, who made it a popular stop for rock acts.

yalebowlyaleuniversity|newhavenct.name: Yale Bowl, Yale University
yalebowlyaleuniversity|newhavenct.extract: Manuscript Society is a senior society at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut. It is reputedly the arts and letters society at Yale.
